exposure: severe acute pain within the first week postpartum
outcome: classification of chronic pelvic and perineal postpartum pain into 7 syndromes (pelvic sensitization, complex regional pain syndrome, pudendal/cluneal neuralgia, neuroma, thoraco-lumbar junction syndrome, myofascial pain, fibromyalgia)
related symptoms (impact on sexual activity, micturition, defecation)
cohort: Forty women who had consulted an algologist or gynecologist at one of six French centers for chronic perineal or pelvic pain (lasting at least 3 months) that they spontaneously linked to their childbirth.
finding: A classification scheme identified various painful disorders in women with chronic postpartum pain, with neuropathic pain present in 77.5% of participants, and neuroma (17 cases), pelvic sensitization (13 cases), and myofascial pain (11 cases) being common findings.
mod_finding: In this specific cohort of women experiencing chronic postpartum pain, a large majority (95%) had a vaginal birth and 90% had a perineal suture.
cross-section timing: At the time of consultation for chronic pain, which was defined as pain lasting at least 3 months postpartum.
